7 can't-miss train trips in Asia

From high-speed shinkansens to routes that are all about taking it slow.

By Katie LockhartJul 29, 20266 minutes read
Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 0:00 Instaread
Sponsored by

Railroad tracks criss-cross the world’s largest continent, offering a train trip for every season and superlative. Whether you're bouncing along aboard a rickety overnight locomotive where sleep is part of the adventure or gliding across the countryside on one of the world's fastest and most sophisticated trains, Asia rewards travelers who slow down enough to watch the scenery unfold. Along the way, you'll pass snowcapped mountains, emerald tea farms, buzzy megacities, remote villages, and dramatic coastlines—all from the comfort of a window seat.

The Vietage, Vietnam

Six hours from Da Nang to Quy Nhon

Built to link two Anantara hotels, this daily train runs Da Nang to Quy Nhon via Nha Trang in two 12-seat carriages, open to anyone.

Three things not to miss:

  • A three-course meal by Anantara chefs.
  • A global coffee menu, including local coconut coffee.
  • A free massage in the onboard spa.

Argo Wilis Panoramic, Indonesia

10 hours from Surabaya to Bandung

Beyond Bali, Java offers a scenic Kereta Api Indonesia ride past rice paddies and palms, with reclining seats and air-conditioning.

Three things not to miss:

  • Prambanan and Borobudur temples, via a stop at Yogyakarta.
  • Bandung's creative cafes and street food at the end of the line.
  • A Bali beach stay, an hour's flight from Surabaya.

Tip: Book the Panoramic carriage, left-side A or B seats.

Ella to Kandy Line, Sri Lanka

Seven hours from Ella to Kandy

Expect waterfalls, tea plantations and mountain views, though the line is closed for repairs until 2027.

Three things not to miss:

  • Ella's Nine Arches Bridge, best seen from the hillside.
  • The Demodara Loop, where the track circles back on itself.
  • St. Clair's Falls, sometimes visible from the train.

Tip: Seats sell out fast, so book well ahead.

Alishan Forest Railway, Taiwan

Five hours from Chiayi City to Alishan Township

This misty 44-mile mountain line crosses about 50 bridges and nearly 80 tunnels, including the world's longest spiral railway.

Three things not to miss:

  • The 1,000-year-old Shuishan Giant Tree, a short walk from Alishan station.
  • Fresh donuts in Fenqihu, where the Number 5 train stops.
  • Ticket release at 6 a.m. Taiwan time, 14 days out.

Tip: Bring a jacket for the high altitude.

Eastern Oriental Express, Malaysia

Three days from Singapore through Malaysia

Belmond's opulent train offers three-night trips or a six-night route through Malaysia, stopping at parks and UNESCO towns.

Three things not to miss:

  • Five treatments at the onboard Dior Spa.
  • Signature cocktails in the piano bar.
  • Penang's street food, reached from Butterworth.

Tokaido Shinkansen, Japan

Under three hours from Tokyo to Kyoto

Japan's most popular bullet-train route links Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Nagoya and Yokohama, passing Mount Fuji at 177 mph.

Three things not to miss:

  • Fuji views from right-side seats heading to Osaka.
  • Convenience-store snacks and drinks before boarding.
  • An easy overnight stay in Kyoto.

Tip: Be on the platform about five minutes early.

Xining to Lhasa, Train Z8991, China

22 hours from Xining to Lhasa, Tibet

One of the world's highest railways, this 1,215-mile sleeper eases riders into Tibet's altitude with daytime mountain views.

Three things not to miss:

  • Tanggula Pass, over 16,640 feet, with onboard oxygen.
  • Tibetan antelope herds in Hohxil from June to August.
  • Longer summer daylight between Golmud and Lhasa.

Tip: Secure a Tibet Travel Permit in advance.
